title: Making A Large Island
summary: Given an n x n binary matrix, you are to determine the size of the largest island that can be formed by changing at most one 0 to a 1.
statement: Given an n x n binary matrix, you are to determine the size of the largest island that can be formed by changing at most one 0 to a 1. An island is defined as a group of 4-directionally connected 1s.
constraints: grid is square and contains zeros and ones.
Change at most one zero to one and return the largest four-connected island area.
hints: A flipped zero joins each distinct neighboring island once.
Label existing islands and store their areas, then evaluate every zero.
Labels make connectivity explicit and the set prevents double-counting one island touching from multiple sides.
editorial: Labels make connectivity explicit and the set prevents double-counting one island touching from multiple sides.

tests.explanation: Flipping either zero joins both diagonal land cells through the new cell, giving area three.
Flipping the final zero fills the 2-by-2 island for area four.
